question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says "When the cast or sorted door refuses to write the red's ticket, run_proof raises an unticketed trouble instead of writing a ticket, then re-raises so the run fails loudly", but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline clause requires 'each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds, unless one is already open for it.' The ticket's implementation explicitly does NOT write the ticket when a door refuses. The ticket acknowledges this conflict in its constraints: 'it is the record that the outline was not met, the red still needs its ticket.' Both cannot stand: either the ticket is written per the outline, or it is not written (and a trouble replaces it) per the ticket's implementation.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands and the ticket now says how it is met. The ticket never writes a trouble in place of the red's ticket: every run tries the ticket, a refusal leaves the red new so the next run tries again, and the trouble (naming the lacks the refusal used to lose) clears when one succeeds. Falsifier clause 4 proves the retry.
